blueprint_topic: Management of Care — patient-centered shared decision-making for advanced CKD treatment pathways
stem: A client with advanced chronic kidney disease asks how future treatment choices should be discussed if kidney failure progresses. Which nursing response best reflects current guidance?

options.A: Review kidney-replacement and comprehensive conservative-care options, explore the client's goals and preferences, and coordinate an informed individualized decision.
options.B: Have the team identify its preferred kidney-replacement modality first, then focus education on that option so the client has a simpler treatment decision.
options.C: Discuss dialysis and transplantation during planning, then introduce comprehensive conservative care if the client later becomes ineligible for kidney-replacement therapy.
options.D: Base the future pathway mainly on kidney-function and laboratory thresholds, then incorporate the client's goals after the treatment approach has been selected.

rationale: A is correct. KDIGO 2024 Practice Point 5.3.1 supports access to a patient-centered multidisciplinary team that provides education and counseling about different kidney-replacement-therapy modalities and transplant options. Practice Point 5.5.1 states that people with CKD should be informed about both KRT and comprehensive conservative care, and Practice Point 5.5.2 supports comprehensive conservative management for people who choose not to pursue KRT. KDIGO also states in Practice Point 5.4.1 that dialysis initiation is based on a composite assessment that includes symptoms, signs, quality of life, preferences, GFR, and laboratory abnormalities rather than kidney-function thresholds alone. B is incorrect because it narrows education around a team-preferred modality before informed patient-centered discussion. C is incorrect because comprehensive conservative care is a recognized option to discuss, not an option reserved for later KRT ineligibility. D is incorrect because current guidance incorporates preferences and other clinical factors into decision-making rather than selecting the pathway primarily from kidney-function/laboratory thresholds and adding goals afterward.
educational_objective: Support advanced-CKD decisions by providing balanced education about kidney-replacement and comprehensive conservative-care options and integrating the client's informed goals and preferences with multidisciplinary clinical assessment.
source_document_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
source_version_date: Published 2024; current KDIGO CKD guideline suite rechecked 2026-08-20. KDIGO's March 17, 2026 focused update is limited to Chapter 3; this item relies on Chapter 5.
source_locator: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline — summary of recommendation statements/practice points, printed pages S167-S168/PDF file pages 52-53. Practice Point 5.3.1: enable access to a patient-centered multidisciplinary care team including education/counseling about different KRT modalities and transplant options. Practice Point 5.4.1: initiate dialysis based on a composite assessment including symptoms, signs, QoL, preferences, GFR, and laboratory abnormalities. Practice Point 5.5.1: inform people with CKD about options for KRT and comprehensive conservative care. Practice Point 5.5.2: support comprehensive conservative management for people who choose not to pursue KRT. The March 17, 2026 focused-update announcement targets Chapter 3, not Chapter 5.
source_claim_supported: Current KDIGO guidance supports patient-centered multidisciplinary education about KRT and comprehensive conservative care, explicitly recognizes conservative management as an option when KRT is not pursued, and includes patient preferences within treatment decisions rather than relying on kidney-function thresholds alone.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Advocacy, Client Rights, Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Referrals, Case Management, and Continuity of Care: provide/clarify treatment information, support informed client decisions and preferences, coordinate interdisciplinary services, and integrate client goals into the plan of care.
pdf_visual_verification: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline printed page S167/PDF file page 52 was visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20 and showed Practice Point 5.3.1. Printed page S168/PDF file page 53 was visually verified and showed Practice Points 5.4.1, 5.5.1, and 5.5.2. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care advocacy/collaboration content had been visually verified earlier in this audit session.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'advanced CKD shared decision KRT comprehensive conservative care patient preferences multidisciplinary education' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the advanced-CKD treatment-choice construct but removed the uniquely long key and one-size-fits-all distractors. The revised alternatives test realistic errors involving team-preferred modality framing, delaying comprehensive conservative-care discussion until KRT ineligibility, and allowing laboratory thresholds to select the pathway before client goals are integrated.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly integrates patient-centered multidisciplinary education, KRT/conservative-care options, and informed client goals/preferences.
option_audit.B: Plausible team-preference framing error; incorrect because education and decision support should not be narrowed around a predetermined team-preferred KRT modality.
option_audit.C: Plausible sequencing error; incorrect because KDIGO identifies comprehensive conservative care as an option to inform people about, not merely a fallback after KRT ineligibility.
option_audit.D: Plausible threshold-driven error; incorrect because KDIGO includes preferences, symptoms, signs, QoL and other factors rather than choosing the pathway primarily from GFR/laboratory data.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four alternatives contain comparable decision-making detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel approaches to advanced-CKD treatment discussion.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after KDIGO source-based audit and targeted repository search.

independent_second_pass: Fresh adversarial pass rechecked KDIGO 2024 Chapter 5 Practice Points 5.3.1, 5.4.1, 5.5.1 and 5.5.2; visual verification of S167-S168; 2026 focused-update scope limited to Chapter 3; NCSBN advocacy/collaboration fit; all four alternatives; medical-suitability versus team-preference framing; conservative-care timing; threshold-driven decision error; cueing; ambiguity; and near-duplicate risk. No unresolved conflict remains.
